{"file_path":"<path>","content":"# File-type filtering in `ignore::types`

ripgrep's `-t/--type` filtering lives in `crates/ignore/src/types.rs`, with the
built-in type list in `crates/ignore/src/default_types.rs`. This module is
independent of gitignore matching (`crates/ignore/src/gitignore.rs`) and glob
overrides (`crates/ignore/src/overrides.rs`); the three are combined only in
`crates/ignore/src/dir.rs`, at the point where a directory walk decides
whether to descend into or skip a path.

## Representing a type definition

A file type is a `FileTypeDef`: a `name: String` plus a `globs: Vec<String>`
(`types.rs:146`). There is no glob compilation at this stage — `FileTypeDef`
stores the raw glob strings, and `Clone + Eq + PartialEq` are derived so
definitions can be compared and copied cheaply. The public accessors
`name()` and `globs()` are how `--type-list` prints each type (see
`crates/core/main.rs:332`, which iterates `args.types().definitions()`).

Definitions are accumulated in a `TypesBuilder`, which holds a
`HashMap<String, FileTypeDef>` keyed by type name plus a separate
`Vec<Selection<()>>` for which types the caller wants to filter on
(`types.rs:305`). Three ways to populate the map:

- `add(name, glob)` pushes one glob onto the `FileTypeDef` for `name`,
  creating it if absent. `name` must be non-`"all"` and every character must
  be `is_alphanumeric()`, or it returns `Error::InvalidDefinition`
  (`types.rs:417`). This is why `--type-add 'foo-bar:*.x'` is rejected — the
  hyphen isn't alphanumeric.
- `add_def(spec)` parses ripgrep's colon-delimited type-definition string,
  used directly by `--type-add`. Two shapes are accepted, split on `:`
  (`types.rs:442`):
  - `name:glob` (2 parts) — a plain definition.
  - `name:include:other,names` (3 parts, middle literal `"include"`) — copies
    every glob from each named existing type into `name`. `add_def` checks
    all referenced names exist *before* adding anything, so a bad include
    fails atomically rather than partially populating `name`.
- `add_defaults()` walks the `DEFAULT_TYPES` table and calls `add` for every
  `(names, globs)` pair, so a single glob list can be registered under
  several aliases (e.g. `bat` and `batch` both map to `*.bat`,
  `cs`/`csharp` both to `*.cs`).

`clear(name)` removes a type's definition entirely (`--type-clear`); it's a
plain `HashMap::remove` with no effect on selections already pushed.

`select(name)` and `negate(name)` don't touch `types` at all — they append a
`Selection::Select(name, ())` or `Selection::Negate(name, ())` to
`self.selections` (`types.rs:381`, `:395`). The `()` payload is filled in at
build time; passing `name == "all"` expands to one selection per key
currently in the map, which is why `--type=all` behaves as "select every
type registered so far" rather than a literal type named `all` — and why its
effect depends on definitions added *before* it on the command line.

## Building the matcher

`TypesBuilder::build()` (`types.rs:322`) is where selections and definitions
turn into an actual matcher. For each `Selection` in order, it looks up the
named `FileTypeDef`, compiles every one of its globs with
`GlobBuilder::new(glob).literal_separator(true).build()`
(`globset`), and adds the compiled glob to a shared `GlobSetBuilder`. Two
side tables are built in lockstep: `glob_to_selection: Vec<(usize, usize)>`
maps a glob's index in the final `GlobSet` back to `(selection index, glob
index within that def)`, and `has_selected` records whether *any* selection
is a `Select` (as opposed to only `Negate`s). A reference to unknown type
returns `Error::UnrecognizedFileType` — this is the runtime counterpart to
`add_def`'s ahead-of-time check for `include:`.

The result is a `Types` struct: the sorted `defs`, the resolved
`selections` (now holding `FileTypeDef` instead of `()`), `has_selected`,
`glob_to_selection`, the compiled `GlobSet`, and a `Pool<Vec<usize>>` used as
scratch space for match results so `matched()` doesn't allocate per call.

`literal_separator(true)` is a real behavioral choice: it means `*` in a
type's glob won't cross a `/`, so `*.rs` matches `foo.rs` and `src/foo.rs`
(matching is against the file name only, see below) but a hypothetical
`src/*.rs` glob wouldn't match `src/sub/foo.rs`.

## Matching

`Types::matched(path, is_dir)` (`types.rs:261`) is the entry point. Directories
never match (types apply to files) and an empty glob set short-circuits to
`Match::None`. Otherwise it extracts just the file name via
`pathutil::file_name` — type globs never see directory components — and
queries the `GlobSet`. `GlobSet::matches_into` can report multiple matching
globs; `Types` takes `matches.last()`, i.e. the *last-added* (highest
index) match, as the highest-precedence one. Because globs are added to the
builder in `self.selections` order, later `--type`/`--type-not` flags on the
command line win over earlier ones for the same file.

Once the winning glob's `(isel, _)` is known, `sel.is_negated()` decides the
outcome: a negated selection matching means `Match::Ignore`, otherwise
`Match::Whitelist`. If nothing in the `GlobSet` matched at all, the fallback
is `Match::Ignore` when `has_selected` is true (some `--type` was given, so
anything not of that type is out) or `Match::None` when only `--type-not`
selections exist (nothing is explicitly whitelisted, so stay neutral and let
other matchers decide).

## Where it fits in a directory walk

`Types` alone doesn't decide whether ripgrep searches a file — `dir.rs`'s
`Ignore::matched` composes it with overrides and ignore files, in a fixed
precedence: overrides (`-g/--glob`) first and decisive either way, then
gitignore-style ignore rules (short-circuiting only on `Ignore`, since a
gitignore *whitelist* result still needs to survive type filtering), then
`Types::matched` last (`dir.rs:376`–`408`). A `Whitelist` from ignore rules
is held in a local and only returned if types don't override it. This is
also documented at the flag level: `-t/--type`'s long doc says explicitly
that it "has lower precedence than both the `--glob` flag and any rules
found in ignore files" (`crates/core/flags/defs.rs:6795`).

## What a contributor needs to know

- **CLI flags are thin.** `-t/--type`, `--type-not`, `--type-add`,
  `--type-clear` each just push a `TypeChange` variant (`Select`, `Negate`,
  `Add`, `Clear`) onto `LowArgs::type_changes`
  (`crates/core/flags/lowargs.rs:749`), preserving command-line order. The
  actual `TypesBuilder` is assembled once, in `crates/core/flags/hiargs.rs`'s
  `types()` function: `add_defaults()` first, then every `TypeChange`
  replayed in order. Interleaving matters — `--type-clear rust --type-add
  'rust:*.rs'` behaves differently from the flags reversed.
- **`Error::InvalidDefinition` vs `Error::UnrecognizedFileType`.** The former
  is a malformed `add_def` string or a non-alphanumeric name, caught at
  `add`/`add_def` time; the latter is a `select`/`negate` (or `include:`
  reference) naming a type that was never defined, caught at `build()` or
  `add_def()` time respectively. Preserve that split if you touch validation
  — the difference is user-visible in error messages.
- **Adding a default type** means editing `DEFAULT_TYPES` in
  `default_types.rs`, which the module doc comment asks contributors to keep
  lexicographically sorted and wrapped to 79 columns. Duplicate glob patterns
  across aliases (`bat`/`batch`, `cs`/`csharp`) are intentional, not
  redundancy to clean up.
- **Matching is name-only.** Any change that makes `Types::matched` consider
  directory components would be a behavioral break; it currently strips the
  path down to `file_name` before touching the `GlobSet`.
- **Precedence is encoded twice**: once operationally in
  `Ignore::matched` (`dir.rs`), and once in the `--type` flag's own
  documentation string. If you change the composition order in `dir.rs`,
  update `defs.rs`'s `doc_long` for `Type` to match — nothing enforces they
  stay in sync.
- **`Types` is `Clone`-cheap by design.** The `Arc<Pool<Vec<usize>>>` scratch
  buffer and the pre-built `GlobSet` mean a `Types` can be shared across
  worker threads in a parallel walk without rebuilding; don't reintroduce
  per-call allocation in `matched()` without checking the pool's still doing
  its job.
"}

It covers, all grounded in `crates/ignore/src/types.rs`, `default_types.rs`, `dir.rs`, and the CLI wiring in `crates/core/flags/`:
- How `FileTypeDef`/`TypesBuilder` represent type definitions (`add`, `add_def`, `add_defaults`, `clear`, `select`/`negate`)
- How `build()` compiles globs into a `GlobSet` with precedence bookkeeping (`glob_to_selection`, `has_selected`)
- How `Types::matched` resolves precedence and negation at match time
- How this composes with overrides and ignore files in `dir.rs`'s fixed precedence order
